is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles funestus s.l. as malaria vectors in the DRC.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports the frequency of the Vgsc-1014F (kdr-west) mutation in Anopheles gambiae s.l. (page 6, Fig. 2).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Fig. 2 on page 6 provides the frequency of the Vgsc-1014F mutation for five sites, with the total number of mosquitoes genotyped (n) provided for each site.

african_field_population.evidence: The study collected mosquitoes from eight sentinel sites in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) (page 2, Table 1).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original entomological data collected between 2013 and 2016.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study provides specific sentinel sites (e.g., Lodja, Kabondo, Kingasani) and GPS coordinates in Table 1 (page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study reports collection years for susceptibility testing (2013-2016) and HLC (2015-2016), which are clearly defined.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new, original entomological monitoring conducted by the authors between 2013 and 2016.

supplement.evidence: The required genotype data (frequency and sample size) is provided in Fig. 2 on page 6.

assessment.summary: This study monitored insecticide resistance and biting behavior of malaria vectors in eight sentinel sites across the DRC between 2013 and 2016. It reports high frequency of the Vgsc-1014F mutation in Anopheles gambiae s.l. in several sites and widespread resistance to permethrin and DDT, while susceptibility to pirimiphos-methyl was maintained.
